questions: When a column contains a mix of numeric and non-numeric values, does the function treat non-numeric values as NaN and ignore them, or does it treat them as zero?
If a column contains only numeric values, but some are NaN due to missing values from uneven tuples, does np.nanmean ignore those NaN values, or does it propagate NaN?
Should the function handle complex numbers or only int/float? The prompt says 'numeric values' but reference uses isinstance(val, (int, float)).
When unzipping uneven tuples, are missing values filled with NaN for all positions beyond the shortest tuple, or is there a different fill strategy?
If a column has all NaN values (from missing or non-numeric), does the function return np.nan or skip the column? The prompt says set to np.nan if all non-numeric, but missing values are NaN.
Does the function treat boolean values (True/False) as numeric (since they subclass int) or as non-numeric?
Should the output list length equal the maximum tuple length in input, or only include columns with at least one numeric value?
Is the mean calculated as a floating-point number even if all numeric values are integers, or should it preserve integer type?
